output.summary: FY2026 records mostly reflect a commodity price rally: revenue rose 46.5% while bushels fell 0.9%, and the cooperative ranked 8th of 23 on revenue growth and 10th on net savings growth. The 6% cost-per-bushel gain comes from maintenance cuts. Deferred work orders tripled to $1.26M, and the Harlan Junction dust and bearing hazards drew an insurer deadline of 21 November. Drying and grading knowledge sits with one person near retirement and is undocumented. The expansion draft assumes FY2026 prices and unsourced throughput. Fix the safety hazards, start succession, and defer the vote until the case is rebuilt on normalized prices. Do not freeze maintenance spending. Employees report concerns freely, but management does not act on them.
